must_fix: Reconstruct the taste basket from a Qloo series with genuine weekly variation (not piecewise-constant `/v2/trending` levels with a frozen newest ~8 weeks) so the regressor moves in most of the 102 estimation weeks instead of the current median of 29.

Recalibrate or reinterpret the dispersion test: the observed spread (805) sits below the noise floor (1,869) and the null mean (1,352), which with weakly identified per-name betas indicates attenuation/miscalibration, not homogeneity; report it as inconclusive or use simulation-based SEs that incorporate generated-regressor error.

Replace the intersection-union plus refit-interval grade with a power-aware rule (or publish the minimum detectable effect for 35 out-of-sample weeks) so a real but modest cultural effect is not automatically suppressed.

Disclose on every per-name holding page that the cultural beta is identified off at most 31 active weeks and that the cross-sectional dispersion test found no excess heterogeneity, so the column is not mistaken for a differentiated signal.
method_objections: Dispersion test: spread 805 < noise floor 1,869 < null mean 1,352; with per-name betas identified off a median of 29 active weeks of a piecewise-constant regressor, estimates are attenuated and standard errors inflated, so the variance comparison is biased toward homogeneity and 'no detectable heterogeneity' is not established.

The cultural regressor is not a weekly return in practice: `/v2/trending` is piecewise constant and the newest ~8 weeks are frozen, so the cultural beta is estimated from rare step changes rather than a persistent weekly taste channel.

The intersection-union rule with a refit interval on only 35 out-of-sample weeks has very low power (CI [−2.12, +0.64]); it would fail to detect a real effect smaller than roughly 2 points, so NO SIGNAL is a low-power conclusion, not evidence of absence.

The pooled panel reports two nominally significant sub-sector slopes (restaurants t −2.12, apparel t 2.08) that fail Bonferroni 0.0045, and the per-name-market variant eliminates even those (largest t 1.27); presenting them without the multiple-testing burden reads as noise.
overstatements: Phrase: 'genuine heterogeneity between names is not detectable' — correction: the test found no excess dispersion, but the below-noise spread signals attenuation/miscalibration under weak identification, so homogeneity is not established; use 'no excess dispersion detected; the test cannot distinguish homogeneity from attenuation.'

Phrase: 'the spread is no larger than noise, and if anything smaller' — correction: the lower tail (p 0.791) does not establish smaller-than-noise spread; it flags that the variance estimator is inconsistent with the reported standard errors under the null; use 'the observed spread is below the noise floor, inconsistent with a correctly specified variance estimator.'

Phrase: 'it killed the cross-sectional fallback rather than supporting it' — correction: the test was underpowered and likely biased toward the null by shrinkage; it did not falsify heterogeneity; use 'the test failed to detect excess dispersion and is consistent with attenuation from weak identification.'
verdict.dispersion_verdict: No — the construction is not valid as a kill; comparing raw beta variance to mean squared standard error with weakly identified, attenuated per-name betas (median 29 active weeks) biases the spread downward and inflates standard errors, so 'no detectable heterogeneity' is not established; at most the test is inconclusive and the below-noise spread signals miscalibration rather than homogeneity.
verdict.best_next_model_construction: Keep the pre-registered falsification design and intersection-union rule, but rebuild the taste basket from a Qloo endpoint with non-frozen, genuinely weekly variation so the regressor moves in most estimation weeks, then re-run the per-name and panel regressions with the same windows and nulls.
verdict.headline_rewrite: Qloo taste adds no measurable weekly risk to SPY beta across 80 consumer names: a pre-registered null result, not a factor.
verdict.judge_60s: A judge skimming for 60 seconds will likely misread the per-name cultural beta column as a differentiated signal and the 'NO SIGNAL' grade as a formatting choice, when the taste basket moves in only about 29 of 102 weeks (median), the newest Qloo weeks are frozen, and the dispersion test shows the per-name spread is below the noise floor—so the column is mostly estimation error with no cross-sectional meaning.

must_fix: Print a power statement next to the dispersion result: the minimum cross-sectional sd of true betas this test could detect given a median of 29 active weeks and SEs of the observed width. Without it, 'no detectable heterogeneity' is unreadable as either a kill or a pass.

Reconcile the three inconsistent variance figures (observed 805, mean-squared-SE 1,869, independent-rotation null mean 1,352). The rotation null mean exceeding the analytic noise benchmark by 55% shows one of the two benchmarks is miscalibrated; identify which before citing either.

Surface the Qloo-vs-peer-basket ablation side by side in the product UI. Right now the desk's own no-Qloo control performs comparably out of sample, and a judge who digs finds the Qloo delta unmeasurable; show the comparison deliberately rather than letting it be discovered.

State on the read page that NO SIGNAL is conditional on a 102-week window with a piecewise-constant source of 19-31 active weeks, and give the detectable-effect bound explicitly (~2 pts on the refit interval).
method_objections: Dispersion test reading: the construction (independent rotation, both tails) is defensible, but 'no detectable heterogeneity' is only non-detection. With median 29 of 102 active weeks the per-name SEs are wide, the mean-squared-SE benchmark inherits that width, and the test's power against realistic heterogeneity (sd 0.3-0.5) is unknown. Spread 805 < null mean 1,352 is as consistent with overestimated SEs under thin identification as with genuinely homogeneous names. The reading is correct only as stated, not as a kill.

Intersection-union rule: valid but conservative. The rotation and permutation nulls are computed on the same dataset and are positively correlated, so demanding both at p <= 0.10 pushes the effective level well below 0.10; a real effect of the magnitude this window could resolve would likely fail the rule too. Acceptable for a falsification-first desk, but the team should state the rule suppresses power, not just that it is stricter.

Grading on the refit interval [-2.12, +0.64]: refitting inside each bootstrap draw is honest, but the resulting interval is so wide that the data cannot distinguish 'no effect' from 'large negative effect.' The FAIL/NO SIGNAL distinction therefore rests on a point estimate (mean OOS -0.05) that has essentially no standing; the distinction is semantic, and the desk should not lean on it.

Permutation p-values on within-delta-R-squared for a piecewise-constant series: permuting week labels destroys the serial structure imposed by the refresh cadence (71 of 106 weeks at exactly zero). The null distribution may be mis-calibrated in the direction of ease; a block permutation respecting the cadence would confirm the 0.898/0.778/0.923 figures.
overstatements: "kill of the team's own fallback story" / "came back a kill" — upper tail p 0.212 with a conservative, low-power benchmark is non-detection, not a kill; correct to 'the dispersion test found no evidence of heterogeneity and has unknown power.'
"3 priced names lack prices (WBD, EA, K)" — contradiction in terms; these are resolved names that lack prices. As written the 80-priced count is not internally consistent.

"the factor was looked for and not detectable at this window length" adjacent to "explicitly not FAILS (measured negative, interval clear)" — the refit interval is not clear of zero on either side, so neither grade's parenthetical describes the data cleanly; the correction is that NO SIGNAL and FAILS are not distinguishable at this power.
verdict.dispersion_verdict: No — the construction is sound but the reading overreaches: with a median of 29 active weeks the SE benchmark makes the test conservative toward a kill, and the 805/1,869/1,352 discrepancy shows the null variance is unstable, so the correct statement is 'heterogeneity not detected' rather than 'the fallback is dead.'
verdict.best_next_model_construction: Keep the current construction, but add a power-calibrated dispersion test: simulate heterogeneity (sd 0.3 and 0.5) through the same rotation machinery conditional on each name's observed active-week pattern, and report the smallest detectable sd. That converts the kill from an assertion into a bounded claim and tells the judge exactly what a longer window would buy.
verdict.headline_rewrite: Taste-basket returns show no measurable cross-sectional or time-series association with consumer equity returns beyond the market over 2024-2026, and the desk reports the exact effect sizes and heterogeneity this window cannot exclude.
verdict.judge_60s: A judge will most likely misread NO SIGNAL as 'Qloo data does nothing here' — when the desk's own peer-basket ablation, which uses no Qloo data, performs comparably out of sample, that reading is hard to refute from the current surface. The 60-second skim needs to see why a no-Qloo control is the honest test and what Qloo uniquely provides (entity resolution, affinity weighting, exclusivity by construction), or the CTO will conclude the pipeline is Qloo-decorated rather than Qloo-dependent.
